findings.title: Migration crashes when `embed_category` site setting row is absent
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. On the vast majority of sites the `embed_category` setting was never set (no row in site_settings) or doesn't match a category name, so the result set is empty and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the migration (and the whole deploy). Same risk on line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Use `.first` with a nil check / COALESCE instead.

findings.title: Un-escaped interpolation of site setting value into INSERT
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates the old `embeddable_hosts` setting value straight into SQL. A host containing a single quote (data entered by an admin, or garbage left in the settings table) breaks the statement or allows arbitrary SQL execution during migration. Use `quote()`/bind parameters.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` can silently drop an existing table
findings.body: `force: true` issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If this migration is ever re-run, or a table named embeddable_hosts already exists, existing data is destroyed without warning. Drop the `force: true` option for a forward migration.

findings.title: Migrated host values are not normalized, so embedding breaks after upgrade
findings.body: Old `embeddable_hosts` values could be of the form `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234` (the old code explicitly stripped schemes). The migration inserts the raw lines, bypassing the model's before_validation that strips scheme and path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `URI(referer).host`, so rows like `http://example.com` will never match and previously-working embeds will start raising InvalidAccess after the upgrade.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. Creating/validating an EmbeddableHost with a nil host (e.g. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or the admin controller when `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing) raises NoMethodError on nil instead of producing a validation error / 400. Guard with `return if host.blank?`. `sub!` also mutates the caller's string in place, which can raise on frozen string literals.

findings.title: record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host
findings.body: The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but `host` comes from `URI(x).host` without `.downcase`. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `EvilTrout.com`, which never equals the lower-cased column value, so a legitimately configured host is rejected (embedding returns InvalidAccess). Downcase the parameter.

findings.title: Unknown id causes a 500 instead of 404 in update/destroy
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil; `save_host(nil)` then calls `nil.host =` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 error. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`) so a deleted/invalid id yields a proper 404.

findings.title: `update` is a no-op but is presented as a save action
findings.body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores the request body entirely and just re-serializes the current state. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` and will appear to succeed while persisting nothing. Either implement the update or remove the route/action so admins aren't misled.

findings.title: `*_ids` hydration crashes on null or non-array values
findings.body: The new branch does `obj[k].map(...)` whenever a key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with a plural suffix. If a serializer emits `foo_ids: null` (common for empty/absent associations) or a scalar, this throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole payload. Guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])` / a null check; note `hydrated || []` after the map never helps because map always returns an array.

findings.title: No presence validation on category_id while the column is NOT NULL
findings.body: The migration declares `category_id` NOT NULL but the model has no `validates_presence_of :category_id`. Only the admin controller patches in `uncategorized_category_id`; any other code path (fabricators, console, future callers) that saves without a category raises a raw ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation instead of a validation error.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped between files
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the category fabricators and `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the embeddable_host fabricator. It works because all fabricator files are loaded, but it makes the definitions unfindable by name and will confuse anyone editing category fabricators. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: New host with no chosen category shows no category badge
findings.body: When adding a host without picking a category, `categoryId` stays null; the server defaults to uncategorized, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` (undefined), so the row renders an empty category cell until a reload. Use the category_id returned by the server response instead of the local `categoryId`.
